chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who fabricates (accuses) against a man, so he excuses him from it, then he wants to flog him after the excusing. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for him to flog him after the excusing.'

key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: to fabricate an accusation or charge

ai.seo_question: Can an accuser retract their forgiveness and demand flogging after initially excusing the accused?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that once an accuser voluntarily waives the right to the penalty (whether hadd or ta'zir), the ruling becomes final and he cannot retract his forgiveness to enforce the punishment later. This principle underscores the accuser's exclusive right to the penalty in private disputes, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence between rights of individuals (haqq al-adam) and rights of God (haqq Allah). The ruling ensures legal stability by preventing the accuser from arbitrarily revoking their concession after the accused has relied on it.
